lead: Vehicle graphics do not have to cover every panel to communicate a business identity. A well-placed logo, short service description and clear contact route can give a work vehicle a coordinated appearance. For New York teams, that may be a useful starting point when vehicles vary in color or body style. Vision Graphics can help organize a repeatable graphic set around the space available, while accounting for panel shapes, existing markings and the condition of each vehicle before production is planned.

sections.html: Separate letters and decals leave the vehicle visible, so contrast is essential. Review each design against the actual paint color and avoid small details that disappear from a distance. The rear may need a simpler arrangement than the sides because its usable space is different.

Keep approved artwork, placement drawings and vehicle-specific dimensions together. This makes replacements and future additions easier to scope. Before each installation, confirm the actual vehicle, surface condition and any changes to the contact information or branding.

items.p: Apply names and short messages as separate characters.
Present full-color brand artwork within a defined graphic area.
Develop consistent elements that can be adapted to different body styles.

items.q: Are graphics a lower-coverage alternative to a wrap?
items.a_html: Yes. The design can focus on selected areas while using the existing vehicle color as the background.
Existing graphics and adhesive should be assessed. Removal and surface preparation may be needed for a sound result.
